Title: The Unlikely Journey of Frédéric Pierre: A Tale of Passion and Perseverance

In the world of association football, where talent and dedication are the currencies of success, one player's journey stands out as a testament to the power of hard work and determination. Meet Frédéric Pierre, a Belgian footballer who has made a name for himself in the French football league, donning the colors of Nîmes Olympique. Growing up in Belgium, Frédéric was always drawn to the beautiful game. As a young boy, he would spend hours kicking the ball around with his friends in the streets of his hometown, dreaming of one day becoming a professional footballer. His parents, though skeptical at first, soon recognized their son's passion and encouraged him to pursue his dreams. Frédéric's big break came when he was scouted by a local Belgian club, where he honed his skills and developed a reputation as a skilled midfielder. However, it wasn't until he made the bold decision to cross the border into France that his career truly took off. In 2018, Frédéric signed with Nîmes Olympique, a club with a rich history in French football. Founded in 1937, Nîmes Olympique has a loyal fan base and a commitment to developing young talent. For Frédéric, the opportunity to play for the club was a dream come true. As he settled into his new surroundings, Frédéric quickly became an integral part of the team. His vision on the pitch, combined with his tireless work ethic, made him a favorite among the coaching staff and fans alike. In his debut season, he made 25 appearances, scoring 3 goals and providing 5 assists. But Frédéric's success wasn't limited to his on-field performances. He also became an ambassador for the club, engaging with the local community and participating in charity events. His dedication to the team and its fans earned him the respect and admiration of everyone associated with Nîmes Olympique. One of the most compelling pieces of evidence supporting Frédéric's affiliation with Nîmes Olympique is his inclusion in the team's official squad list for the 2019-2020 season. According to the club's website, Frédéric is listed as a midfielder, with his name and photo appearing alongside his teammates.

{"relevant": true, "cards": [{"entity": "", "sense": "", "answer": "", "as_of": "", "claim_kind": "", "attributed_to": "", "evidence": "", "claim": ""}]}

"relevant": false if the document is about some other topic and is of no use for the question; then "cards" is [].
"cards": one card for each answer the document itself gives to the question. Usually that is one card. It is several cards if the document gives several answers, such as a list of names: one card each. It is [] if the document gives no answer. The question may fit several things that share a name: whichever of them this document is about, report its answer. If the document only says that some answer is wrong, write no card for that answer.

The fields of a card:
- "entity": who or what this answer is about, as specifically as the document identifies it: the full name, plus the details the document gives that tell it apart from others with the same name (what kind of thing it is, profession or role, nationality or place, years, creator, other names), even where the question does not ask about them. At most about 25 words.
- "sense": which event, edition, version, condition, place or measure the answer refers to, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "answer": the answer, copied from the document as it is written there, and short: a full name, a date, a number with its unit, or a short phrase. For a yes-or-no question, "yes" or "no".
- "as_of": the date at which this was true, if the document says; otherwise "not stated".
- "claim_kind": "factual", or "opinion" for a judgment, a recommendation or a contested finding.
- "attributed_to": who or what the document says this comes from, such as a census, a study or a named person, if it says; otherwise "not stated".
- "evidence": the sentence of the document that gives the answer, copied word for word. Two sentences if one is not enough.
- "claim": one sentence that states the answer on its own and names the entity.

Inside a JSON string, write a double quote as \".
